title: Mickey One versus Focus
summary: He prefers Mickey One and discusses strings against saxophone.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: The score for Mickey One is much busier.
By necessity I'm sure, because it's a movie, after all.
I think that is a better thing to listen to, though.
You think so? Why is that?
I don't know. I think that he did a better job, I think it's more intense than what he does--I think it's phenomenal what he does on Mickey One.
There is some very intense playing.
I can listen to that, where I can't listen to Focus. (inaudible).
There's a lot more open space--

That's because of the saxophone and the strings. The strings allow the saxophone always to be heard and it's the sort of timbre that doesn't get mixed up and you can hear them too, which is one reason why (inaudible) and why it is used so much.

The only way I could do that was to write them like string quartets; I did that but mostly patterns. If there was a melody they'd have it; sometimes Stan-- I'd give it to Stan and Stan wound his way through that. The same thing on Mickey One.
